extracted.intended_audience: general readers, historians, legal scholars, and students interested in English constitutional documents and 17th-century parliamentary petitions
extracted.subtask_description: A primary-source parliamentary petition (The Petition of Right, 1628) addressed to the King that enumerates legal rights, grievances, and requests for redress under English law of the time.

rubrics_metrics.name: No taxation or tallage without parliamentary consent
rubrics_metrics.description: By statutes (Statutum de Tallagio non Concedendo; statutes in the reigns of Edward I and Edward III) subjects inherit the freedom that they should not be compelled to contribute to any tax, tallage, aid, or other like charge not set by common consent in parliament.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly cites earlier statutes and holds that levies such as tallage, aid, loans, benevolences, or similar impositions require the good will and assent of the representatives (archbishops, bishops, earls, barons, knights, burgesses, and other freemen) — i.e., parliamentary consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: No forced loans, oaths, or compulsion by commissioners
rubrics_metrics.description: Recent commissions and instructions have assembled people in counties and required them to lend certain sums to the Majesty; upon refusal they have had an oath administered not warrantable by the laws or statutes, been constrained to give appearance before the Privy Council, been imprisoned, confined, and otherwise molested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies abuses by commissions, lord lieutenants, deputy lieutenants, commissioners for musters, justices of the peace and others acting by command or direction from the King or Privy Council; prohibits compelling loans or administering unlawful oaths and punishments for refusal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection under the Great Charter (Magna Carta) — lawful judgment and law of the land
rubrics_metrics.description: By the Great Charter of the Liberties of England no freeman may be taken or imprisoned or be disseized of his freehold or liberties, or be outlawed or exiled, or in any manner destroyed, but by the lawful judgment of his peers, or by the law of the land.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Asserts that Magna Carta establishes that deprivation of liberty or property requires lawful judicial process rather than summary or arbitrary executive action.

rubrics_metrics.name: No dispossession, imprisonment, disinheritance, or death without due process
rubrics_metrics.description: Statute in the 28th year of Edward III declared that no man, of what estate or condition, should be put out of his land or tenements, nor taken, nor imprisoned, nor disinherited nor put to death without being brought to answer by due process of law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reiterates statutory protection that civil and criminal penalties affecting life, liberty, or property must follow established legal proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to certify cause for detention — prohibition on arbitrary imprisonment
rubrics_metrics.description: Despite writs of habeas corpus and commands that keepers certify causes of detainer, persons have been returned to prisons with no cause certified, detained by the King's special command signified by the Lords of the Privy Council.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insists that keepers must certify lawful cause for detention when presented under habeas corpus; objects to returns and continued detention without cause simply by royal command.

rubrics_metrics.name: No forced billeting of soldiers or mariners in private houses against inhabitants' wills
rubrics_metrics.description: Great companies of soldiers and mariners have been dispersed into counties and inhabitants against their wills compelled to receive them into their houses and suffer them to sojourn, contrary to the laws and customs and to the great grievance of the people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibits compelling subjects to lodge or entertain military forces in their homes without lawful authority or consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: No summary proceedings by martial law in place of established law
rubrics_metrics.description: By the Great Charter and other laws no man shall be forejudged of life or limb against the form of the Great Charter and the law of the land; yet commissions have been issued empowering commissioners to proceed according to the justice of martial law and by such summary course and order as is used in armies in time of war.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declares that martial law procedures (summary trials/condemnations used in armies) are not an acceptable substitute for the ordinary courts and statutory procedures of the realm when applied domestically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executions under martial law contrary to statutory law are unlawful
rubrics_metrics.description: Some of the Majesty's subjects have been by the said commissioners put to death when, if judged by the laws and statutes of the land, they had deserved death by those laws and statutes also they might, and by no other ought to have been judged and executed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms that taking life via commissions operating under martial law where statutory law governs is improper; executions must conform to the established law of the land.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissions claiming exclusive martial law jurisdiction are contrary to law and enable impunity
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievous offenders have escaped punishments due because officers and ministers have refused or forborne to proceed according to the laws and statutes on pretense that the offenders were punishable only by martial law and by authority of such commissions; such commissions and all others of like nature are wholly and directly contrary to laws and statutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objects to use of commissions as a pretext to avoid ordinary prosecution, resulting in both unlawful punishments and unlawful exemptions; calls such commissions contrary to the realm's laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prayer for remedies — revoke unlawful commissions and prevent future impositions without Parliament
rubrics_metrics.description: They pray that no man hereafter be compelled to make or yield any gift, loan, benevolence, tax, or such like charge, without common consent by act of parliament; that none be called to make answer, or take such oath, or to give attendance, or be confined, or otherwise molested; that soldiers and mariners be removed; that the aforesaid commissions for proceeding by martial law be revoked and annulled; and that no commissions of like nature may issue forth henceforth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets forth concrete remedies sought: a prohibition on levies without parliamentary act, protection from coercive oaths and confinement for refusal, removal of quartered troops, and revocation/annulment and prevention of commissions exercising martial law domestically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration that unlawful awards and proceedings shall have no future consequence and officials must obey the law
rubrics_metrics.description: They pray that the awards, doings, and proceedings to the prejudice of the people in any of the premises shall not be drawn hereafter into consequence or example; and that the King declare his royal will that in the things aforesaid all officers and ministers shall serve according to the laws and statutes of the realm, as they tender the honor of the Majesty and prosperity of the kingdom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests a royal declaration negating precedential effect of unlawful acts and an instruction that officers and ministers obey statutes and common law to protect subjects' comfort and safety.
